title: ASEv4 `Atoms` (based on !3783, !3856, !3857)
body:
This MR cuts out `Atoms` related parts from !3783, !3856, !3857. Credit to @gelzinyte and @jameskermode.

The preceding MRs include also the suggestions for ASEv4 calculators.
For these, as many parts look the same as the ASEv3 correspondence, we will still need efforts to clean up.

To proceed step by step, here I cut out the implementation of ASEv4 `Atoms` together with `CalculationResults`.
These may be easier to review and I believe 80-90% we all can agree.
This is not a suggestion of fixed API; whenever necessary we can update during the ASEv4 development.

@askhl, @ajjackson: Maybe we can chat about this MR in a discussion tomorrow.

Related to !3941 in the sense that the suggested optimizers should hopefully work with ASE4 `Atoms`.

comments.label_reasoning: The comment suggests a parameter type should be `dict | None = None`, implying the current code may not properly handle the None case or has an incorrect type annotation that could lead to null dereference issues.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests a specific type annotation change to use `dict | None = None`.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
I think we need some more formalization of what these things are, what prefixes or suffixes mean.

If they're for namespacing then we should implement them as namespaces rather than by concatenating strings.

Currently the implementation will lose information because prefix, name, and suffix are compiled into a single string, but there's no way to split them into tokens again.

Either we should use a separator (e.g. `.`) or we could do a dict of dicts (proper namespace).  Whatever we do, we can implement an API on top that is effectively namespaces.

But it still smells funny to me that we want complete flexibility while also some things like `numbers` and `positions` are still mandatory.

(In my opinion this is not yet the right time to think about `store()`.)
comments.label_reasoning: The comment raises concerns about lack of formalization, improper namespacing via string concatenation (losing information), and the overall architecture of how prefixes/suffixes/namespaces are organized — all pointing to structural and design issues.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Thank you @askhl for pointing this out! I think I also agree on:

> If they're for namespacing then we should implement them as namespaces rather than by concatenating strings.

So, for example, this will rather be `def store(self, results: CalculationResults, namespace: str)` with also re-designing `self.arrays` and `self.info` to be accessed somehow like `self.arrays[namespace]['positions']`.

Let's consider this in a follow-up MR!

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags multiple concerns: lack of formalization, information loss from string concatenation, and suggests concrete alternatives (separator like `.` or dict of dicts for namespacing).
